static_traits.name: Wei An
static_traits.social_status: Relationships with colleagues are strained due to deadline pressure; has a few close friends to talk about private matters with, but has not discussed work stress with them
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; has not previously received psychotherapy or counseling
static_traits.language_features: Neutral attitude; clear expression, able to describe anxiety and self-doubt; in conversation can identify and respond to the counselor's exploration of thinking patterns

basic_info.main_problem: I believe I am not good at my work as an architect; despite having won awards and praise from my boss, I often miss deadlines, which makes me believe I am not good enough.
basic_info.core_demands: Persistent negative self-talk and self-doubt about work performance have affected my mental health and job satisfaction, so I sought counseling; I hope to view my abilities in a more balanced way, reduce stress, and improve my self-evaluation.
growth_experiences: About a year ago, the client missed a project deadline for the first time; the stress was great and the workload felt overwhelming; afterward, frequent missed deadlines worsened the client's self-doubt and negative self-talk, work performance was affected, relationships with colleagues became strained, and daily life was impacted (disturbed sleep, reduced interest in cooking and fishing).

core_beliefs: I am incompetent / I am not good enough at work
My worth depends on whether I can complete tasks on time

special_situations.event: As a project deadline approaches, sensing it may be delayed
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not finish on time, it means I am completely incompetent / I am a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Works overtime in sprints, tries to improve time management and seeks help from colleagues, but keeps pressuring the self amid anxiety
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: No matter what I do I cannot keep up; I cannot do it well

special_situations.event: Receiving praise from the boss or winning an award for work quality
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: External affirmation is unreliable, others must have overlooked my mistakes
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating positive feedback, emphasizing one's shortcomings to avoid 'being exposed'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They just did not see my mistakes; this praise does not count

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I exert more effort or am more anxious than them, it means my ability is not as good as others
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Imposing higher, more perfect demands on oneself, reinforcing self-criticism
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Others would not struggle like me; I am not as good as them

special_situations.event: After a project is completed on time or achieves good results, reviews performance
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Good outcomes are not a reflection of ability, just luck or an easy task
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Downplaying success, attributing it to external accidental factors rather than one's own ability
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This time was just luck / the project was relatively easy

special_situations.event: Work is of high quality but submitted a few days late (such as a community center project winning an award)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Being late simply equals failure, no matter how high the quality
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Judging self-worth by strict time standards, ignoring positive results
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: No matter how well it is done, if it is late it is worthless

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized as competent and valuable, with the quality of the work and effort genuinely seen and affirmed
core_conflict.fear: Fears failure and being negated, being seen through by others as 'not good enough', and thereby being slighted or humiliated
defense_goal: Reducing the risk of being exposed by self-deprecation and negating positive feedback
Maintaining a sense of control and security through perfection and high standards
Avoids internalizing success as ability in order to lessen anxiety about being evaluated

object_relations.self_representation: An employee who is not good enough and prone to failure
object_relations.object_representation: Picky and insincere judges / praisers (others will overlook mistakes or give hypocritical praise)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor or others give praise and affirmation (mentioning awards, the boss's praise)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client tends to believe others overlook mistakes and that praise is insincere (projecting their own doubts onto others' intentions)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Downplays and questions the validity of praise, with a cautious tone, emphasizing that others 'did not see my mistakes', and attributes success to external factors.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing missed deadlines or needing to evaluate one's own performance
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Treats the rigid standard 'late submission equals failure' as objective truth, using it to explain own incompetence
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Uses 'should / must' sentence patterns to emphasize the importance of being on time, weakening the value of work quality, with a self-critical tone and logical explanations of why late submission makes everything worthless.

manifestations: Living alone且主要与三只狗为伴
Although there are a few close friends, has not expressed work stress to them
Relationships with colleagues strained and distant due to stress
Believing late submission equals failure, thus belittling the significance of high-quality work
After receiving awards and praise, quickly negates their value, regarding them as 'luck' or others not having seen the mistakes
outcomes: Difficulty internalizing a sense of achievement

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Frequently using the rigid self-demand 'I should be able to handle everything perfectly'
Treats 'late submission = failure' as an absolute standard for judging oneself

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: When affirmed or awarded, quickly shifts to emphasizing mistakes and late submission, avoiding direct contact with positive experience
Attributing success to luck rather than one's own ability

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Persistent self-criticism and self-doubt
Evaluating one's own performance with excessive caution; hard to allow imperfection

exception_events.target_problem: When a deadline approaches and strong anxiety appears, the client usually becomes distracted and ultimately misses the deadline.
exception_events.unique_outcome: On a few occasions under high pressure, the client still managed to complete and deliver projects on time; afterward, although they felt it was 'luck', objectively the deadline requirements were met.
exception_events.reason: Different approach: concentrated energy to sprint during peak anxiety and sought colleagues' help (tried in the past), so this time the task was completed before the deadline.

exception_events.target_problem: After a project delay, the client typically thinks they are completely incompetent and overlooks the value of the work.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Although the community center project was submitted a few days late, it ultimately received wide acclaim and won an award, and the quality of the client's work was objectively recognized.
exception_events.reason: Different understanding: the team and reviewers valued outcome quality more; contextual difference: the project's creative and design strengths were fully presented, making the positive value of the outcome outweigh the time delay.

positive_force: High work quality with awards, the boss continually affirming
Having some sprint and completion ability under pressure (having delivered on time)
Can proactively seek help from colleagues
Has some social support resources (a few close friends)
negative_force: Perfectionism and rigid 'should' standards (late submission = failure)
Disqualifying positive feedback and attributing success to luck
As deadlines approach, high anxiety and difficulty concentrating
Sleep disturbance and decreased work-life satisfaction

target_behavior.behavior: As the deadline approaches, shows strong anxiety, difficulty concentrating, and negative self-talk
antecedent: When handling multiple tasks in the workplace
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalized the core belief that 'late submission = failure / incompetence'; catastrophic expectations lead to increased anxiety and decreased concentration; negating success makes it hard for the sense of self-efficacy to improve.
target_behavior.function: Escapes feelings of being criticized and failing, maintains a sense of control through self-reproach (relieves anxiety in the short term but harms long-term performance)
target_behavior.consequence: Missed deadlines increased, relationships with colleagues strained, sleep impaired and enjoyment of life declined, self-doubt worsened
